acceptance: Each un-gated benchmark has live differential coverage and registered compat rules
One PR per benchmark, each opened with make pr-open
context:
Item-specific guardrails: never lift a gate without live differential coverage; never lift several gates in one PR.

Shared SereneDB guardrails: worktree-only repository writes with make agent-write-preflight; explicit-path staging, never git add -A; commit identity check, no attribution trailers; uv only, no new dependency; lazy psycopg import; no credentials in Git, logs, fixtures, or tracker; Mocker never in CI and its timings never published; pin by digest or exact version and record version(); announce long runs and never commit raw logs; code-skill self-review then make pr-preflight and make pr-open, no auto-merge without make pr-ready; durable artifacts carry no tracker IDs or session narrative; stop and report on failed gates, unverified behavior, or unapproved host changes.
description:
The adapter core blocks every benchmark except TPC-H and TPC-DS. SereneDB's DuckDB-derived semantics (implicit casts, IEEE float ops, NULLS LAST, decimal division as float) and its type gaps (no jsonb, inet, or geometric types; time without time zone only partly supported) may silently change other benchmarks' answers. Lift the gates one benchmark at a time: SSB first, then read_primitives, then ClickBench.

Tasks, per benchmark:
1. Translate its DDL and queries; check types and functions against the SereneDB compatibility matrix.
2. Add live differential coverage against DuckDB at the smallest scale.
3. Register any rewrites or skips with reasons.
4. Remove only that benchmark's gate rule and update the docs.
5. If a second adapter by then needs the same sized-string mapping, consider extracting a shared ddl_helpers function in a separate PR.

Decision gates:
- G1 Start only with explicit user priority. One benchmark per PR.
- G2 If a benchmark needs an unsupported type, keep it gated and record the reason in the rule.
